 10/20 Preview – Zuccarello To Return, 12F/6D Expected + Kuemper Off First, Caps Depth, Schedule Normalizes
 By Zach Dooley 
 5 hours ago 
 258 Comments 
 Share This Article 
 Share This Article 
 WHO: Los Angeles Kings (0-4-2) @ Washington Capitals (5-3-0)
 WHAT: 2026-27 NHL Regular Season, Game 7/84
 WHEN: Tuesday, October 20 @ 4:00 PM Pacific
 WHERE: Capital One Arena – Washington, DC
HOW TO FOLLOW: VIDEO: ABTV, DAZN – VIDEO: 830 AM KLAA, ESPN LA App, LA Kings App – TWITTER: @dooleylak & @lakings 
 TODAY’S MATCHUP: The LA Kings open up a five-game roadtrip tonight in the nation’s capital, as they visit the Washington Capitals for a Tuesday-evening showdown. 
 HEAD-TO-HEAD: Kings forward Artemi Panarin has scored at a point-per-game pace in his career against Washington with 38 points (14-24-38) in 38 games played. Six of Panarin’s 14 goals have come on the power play, tied for his most against any one opponent. 
 KINGS VITALS: The Kings held a full-team morning skate today, after yesterday afternoon’s practice in Washington, getting everybody on the ice on back-to-back. days. 
 Looks like goaltender Darcy Kuemper will start the trip opener, against his former team in Washington. Kuemper has a lifetime record of just 2-5-0 versus the Capitals, but brings strong splits into tonight’s game, with a .921 save percentage and a 2.34 goals-against average. 
 Here is tonight’s projected lineup –
 Panarin – Laferriere – Kempe
Moore – Byfield – Zuccarello
Haula – Laughton – Armia
Lee – Helenius – Perry 
 Gustafsson – Clarke
Edmundson – Doughty
Anderson – Dumoulin
 Kuemper
Forsberg
 Looks like forward Mats Zuccarello will return to the lineup tonight against Washington, skating on a line with Trevor Moore and Quinton Byfield. Zuccarello is still on injured reserve and would need to be activated in order to feature tonight, but seems like things are trending in that direction. Based on today’s skate, it looks like Cody Ceci and Taylor Ward will be the odd men out, with the Kings expected to dress 12 forwards and six defensemen, though I suppose that remains to be seen. 
 CAPITALS VITALS: Washington is in the middle of a five-game homestand, which started with wins over Montreal and New Jersey. 
 Per Tom Gulitti of NHL.com, here’s how the hosts lined up last time out, in a 4-2 win over the Devils – 
 Capitals in warmup: Ovechkin-I. Protas-Miroshnichenko Tuch-Strome-Kyrou A.Protas-Jenner-Wilson Beauvillier-Brodzinski-Leonard Chychrun-Liljegren Fehervary-Desharnais Hutson-Holl Thompson (vs. Allen)
 — Tom Gulitti (@TomGulittiNHL) October 17, 2026 
 Washington captain Alexander Ovechkin announced that the 2026-27 season would be his last in the NHL, meaning that tonight will be the final time a Kings/Capitals game in DC will feature number eight. Ovechkin, who became the first player in NHL history to score 900 regular-season goals, led all Washington skaters with three points (1-2-3) in two games played against the Kings last season. 
 Storyline Of The Day – Zucc’n A 
The Kings have missed Mats Zuccarello.
 Well, sort of. They haven’t really had him, so they’ve more so missed what they expected from him and how he impacts the team. Zuccarello did play the first three games of the season but he might not have been quite at 100 percent. After Game 3, the defeat against Florida, the Kings placed Zuccarello on injured reserve, with an undisclosed injury deemed to have a week-to-week timeline. 
 Zuccarello’s injury didn’t keep him off the ice, just out of the lineup. He was skating shortly after the IR designation, first coming with individual work, as he was on the ice early, before the Kings practiced. Then, last week on Tuesday, Zuccarello popped up with the main group for morning skate that night against Edmonton. He practiced on Thursday and Friday and again took the morning skate on Saturday but didn’t play. 
 Peter Laviolette confirmed over the weekend that Zuccarello would travel with the team, to begin a five-game trip on the East Coast. He practiced in full yesterday and I’d call it full, full……not just full. Zuccarello was a “full-contact participant” last week but at the same time, he was probably more in the 80-90 percent participation range, not taking every single drill. Yesterday was a full go and today feels like his return to game action.
 “Everything is trending that way,” Laviolette said of Zuccarello playing tonight. “I think it helps slot things a little bit, but that being said, I think you have to watch his minutes and where he goes. He’s been out for a bit for us, but he’s definitely a guy that can come in and help with regard to the offensive part of the game.”
 With where the Kings are at, there’s not one lineup injection that is simply going to fix things. So, this isn’t suggesting that Zuccarello is a magical antedote. But, if healthy, Zuccarello has produced everywhere he’s been. You want to point to his age, yeah, he’s 39. But, at 38-years-old, he collected 54 points (15-39-54) in 59 games played. The Kings need all the offensive production they can get and Zuccarello, while his minutes will likely be managed at the start, does help.
 “He’s one of those guys who just finds a way onto the scoresheet,” forward Erik Haula said of Zuccarello. “He creates offense. His mind for the game is elite. Usually, guys like that make other people better around him. So, hopefully he’ll come in and kind of spark the offense a little bit, or at least the line that he’s playing on. For sure we’ve missed him.”
 With Zuccarello in, it puts things more into place. The Kings were so depleted last time out that the two-man line in the 11/7 was the second line. The most common linemate for those two players was Artemi Panarin, meaning that the Kings were severely double shifting their top guys. With Zuccarello, it should provide some balance. He slots in with Moore and Byfield, which keeps the third line together, with Haula, Scott Laughton and Joel Armia. 
 As Laviolette mentioned, managing the minutes here is something he’ll keep an eye on. That is why I think the 12/6 alignment makes sense. A little bit of insurance. The current makeup of the team still favors an 11/7 look in my opinion, but if Zuccarello’s workload is of any concern, dressing the extra forward makes sense at the start. 
 Against a team like Washington, every piece of the puzzle helps. The Kings need far more than just one guy right now. But they’ll take every one guy they can get. 
 “His experience, his playmaking ability, he’s so good on the power play and a good guy to have in the room,” forward Scott Laughton added on Zuccarello. “It’s going to be nice to have him back. I think he’ll add a different element to our top six.”
 3 To Watch For – 
– This trip for the Kings begins the first semblance of a regular schedule.
 To this point, including tonight’s game, there have been at least two days off in between games. The rest and practice time element of the early-season schedule should be favorable. The momentum element, by playing games consistently, has not been. Clearly it hasn’t favored the Kings. It’s not an excuse and in looking at the Boston loss, there is no excuse for the third-period showing, with the legs that should have been there. 
 “It’s tough but I mean all the teams go through it during the season, so we’ve been through it now,” defenseman Erik Gustafsson said. “Now, we’re going back to playing every other day, so we just got to show that we’re ready for tonight. We have to change something in this locker room here……but I believe in this team. It’s a great opportunity to show it.”
 If you wanted to look at that direction, the Kings will begin a routine set of games. One day off between each of the next three games, before the trip concludes with a back-to-back, the first of the season. 
 If the Kings were 6-0 not 0-6, we’d be looking at the schedule through a very different lens. When you are losing, and don’t play regularly, those losses sit with you longer. Fewer chances to get back to it and cut the head off the snake. So, the schedule now changes and the team is on the road. It won’t change just due to circumstances, but perhaps they can assist. 
 “Especially when you’re losing, I think you’ve got to sit on it and think about it more often, so it’s nice [to change that up],” Laughton said of the schedule. “I think to get on the road here and play a simple game, be all together, go for dinners and things like that, I think that can help and help us out going forward. We need to start tonight. It needs to happen right away and we’ll go from there.”
 – One of the biggest tests when you play against Washington is a strength in numbers. 
 The Kings haven’t gotten very much in terms of production from the bottom of their lineup, but they’ll need, at the very least, some quality minutes from that group against a team like the Capitals. Washington plays four lines deep. Last time out, forward Ryan Leonard was listed on the fourth line and he’s tied for the team lead in scoring, coming off a 20-goal season in 2025-26. That is without former Kings forward Pierre-Luc Dubois too, who isn’t expected to play today due to illness, but offers another player into an already deep and crowded mix up front.
 Overall, on the Los Angeles front, Scott Laughton is the only player with a 5-on-5 point from the group of Laughton, Armia, Lee, Helenius and Perry. The return of Zuccarello helps there, in that it shuffles Erik Haula into the bottom six and Haula has a couple of points in his account. Getting more from that group, when playing against guys who might play in the top six elsewhere, feels quite important. 
 “There are some areas that we’ve got to find a way to get more traffic in front of the other goalies and just find simpler ways of finding offense,” Haula said. “Those ugly goals that we’ve talked about, we haven’t had too many of them yet, so we have to just create a little bit more traffic and just try to play faster overall. You don’t see a lot of odd-man rushes for us right now. It’s our reads and playing faster.”
 The Capitals spread the minutes around pretty well. The Kings have three forwards – Byfield, Kempe and Panarin – who would handily lead Washington in time on ice up front. The Capitals don’t have a forward in the 20’s this season. Alex Tuch and Tom Wilson lead Washington up front in average TOI at 18:46 apiece. There’s a ton of balance from there, too. That puts the onus on players who will get tougher matchups from a third or fourth line than with most teams. 
 On the road, you don’t get control over the matchups, but it might matter a little bit less against the Capitals than most, because of how deep they are. Whoever is on the ice, it’ll be a tougher matchup. Need to be aware of that. 
 – For the penultimate time, we’ll see the Kings square off with Ovechkin.
 Last season was a pair of unbelievable milestones, as Ovechkin scored his 900th career regular-season goal and the 1,000th goal of his career overall, between the regular season and playoffs. 
 Laviolette had the opportunity to coach Ovechkin during his time in Washington and while there’s only so much you can say about the greatest goalscorer of all time, it’s still pretty special to him what Ovechkin continues to do, even this deep into his career. 
 “I had a good relationship with Ovi, we talked all the time,” Laviolette said. “What people might not know about him – I think a lot of people do, but they might not – is he’s a terrific human being. Obviously, the game itself speaks for what he’s done over his career. But as a human being, he’s right there as well. He’s got an infectious love of the game. I think out of all the players that I’ve coached throughout my career, his love for the game, for his teammates, for being a part of a team and a city……when you get to see that on the inside like I did, maybe you didn’t realize it on the outside. This has been his whole life and he shows that everyday.”
 Kings and Capitals as the roadtrip gets underway. Washington is 4-1-0 this season at home and the Kings are winless in three attempts on the road, with a record of 0-1-2. Start of a five-game trip with a ton of implications on where things could go from here.
